article.dek: Baltimore has named its Thursday night starter, the Thursday line has flipped a long way from its lookahead number, and the board still has not flipped to Week 9.

items.headline: Lead: Joe Fagnano will start Thursday for Baltimore
paragraphs: The morning's big unknown is answered. Head coach Jesse Minter announced Tuesday that undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night against Jacksonville. It will be his first career start, and Baltimore's third starting quarterback this season.

Fagnano practiced Tuesday as a full participant with his right ankle heavily taped and braced. He hurt the ankle Sunday at Buffalo on a low hit, then finished the game, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with an interception and a lost fumble.

Lamar Jackson did not practice with his right thumb injury and is headed for surgery and injured reserve. Tyler Huntley did not practice with his toe injury and is out for Thursday. Baltimore signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad Tuesday to the 53-man roster, and Jake Moody is expected to kick Thursday.
items.takeaway: Fagnano starts Thursday: third Ravens starter this season, ankle braced but a full participant Tuesday.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Jacksonville loses two starters, and its top back is in question
paragraphs: Jacksonville coach Liam Coen confirmed Monday that defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray are out for the rest of the season. Hamilton tore a quadriceps muscle and Murray hurt his elbow in Sunday's 42-7 win over Indianapolis. Both are headed to injured reserve.
Jacksonville running back Bhayshul Tuten did not practice again Tuesday with a foot injury, and his status for Thursday is in question. He is Jacksonville's leading rusher this season.
On the Baltimore side, starting right guard Roger Rosengarten (ankle), starting left guard John Simpson (back), and nose tackle John Jenkins (knee) were limited both days of practice this week.
items.takeaway: Jacksonville loses Hamilton and Murray for the season, Tuten's Thursday status is in question, and three Baltimore linemen were limited both days.

items.headline: Thursday weather in Baltimore: mild, with showers possible late
paragraphs: Thursday night in Baltimore looks mild at kickoff, with temperatures in the mid-60s and a light southwest wind around 5 mph. Showers are possible late in the evening, with about a 50 percent chance of rain late Thursday night.
That is a forecast, not a betting edge. It can still change before kickoff, so check it again Thursday. The game is Jacksonville at Baltimore on Thursday, November 5, at 8:15 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: Mild Thursday night in Baltimore, light wind, showers possible late — check the forecast again before kickoff.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards yet
paragraphs: Read this plainly: the app's board still shows Week 8. It was generated November 2, and a second check this evening confirmed it has not flipped. There are no Week 9 cards, and there is no Jacksonville at Baltimore game on the board at all — so the app has not picked up Fagnano as Thursday's starter yet. Do not look to the board for Thursday's quarterback; the practice reports above are the current word.

The cards still on the board are Monday night's, and they are history now, not live picks. Hit Rate was Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings — the pick the app rates most likely to win. Seattle lost, so that pick lost. Balanced and Value were both Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings, and Chicago won outright, so that pick won. Hit Rate is the likeliest pick, not a promise; the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

When the board flips, Thursday's cards will appear. Until then, if your book already has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Board still on Week 8, no Week 9 cards, Thursday's starter not yet reflected — use the practice reports and run any Thursday price through Check.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: what a push means
paragraphs: A push is a tie against the spread. Nobody wins the bet, and nobody loses it. Your stake comes back.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you bet a team at -3, and that team wins by exactly 3 points. The final margin lands right on the number, so the bet pushes and your stake is returned.

That is why the number matters as much as the team. The same team at -2.5 would have won that bet, and at -3.5 it would have lost it. A push is not a win, and it is not a loss — it is the market calling it exactly even.
items.takeaway: A push means the margin landed exactly on the spread, so your stake comes back — the number you bet matters as much as the team.

items.headline: Thursday's line has flipped a long way since the lookahead
paragraphs: This is the move of the week so far, and it is all quarterback news. The shadow-tracked lookahead for Jacksonville at Baltimore had Baltimore as a 3-point favorite with a total of 48.5. By this morning's snapshot it had flipped to Jacksonville favored by 8.5 to 9.5 points, with the total down to 42.5.

This evening, FanDuel lists Jacksonville -9.5 with a total of 40.5, and Covers' Week 9 board shows the same direction: an opener of Jacksonville -7.5 and a total of 48.5, now Jacksonville -9.5 and 42.5. The market moved with the news that Baltimore is down to its third quarterback.

The app has not caught this move yet — its board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, with no Week 9 cards at all. So do not look to the board for Thursday's price. If your book has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Baltimore -3 and a 48.5 total in the lookahead are gone — Jacksonville is now about a 9.5-point favorite with the total in the low 40s.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The quarterback question is answered, so there is no reason to wait on that news anymore. If your book has a Thursday number you like, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
One thing still to watch: the inactive list lands about 90 minutes before kickoff Thursday. If anything changes there, run your price through Check again before you act.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here. Settlement in the tracker is manual, and it only works if you are honest with yourself — log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Thursday game? Thursday check. Run your book's Thursday price through Check, and re-check if the inactive list changes anything.
